key_insight: Auxiliary-space multigrid preconditioners remove the need for nested conforming coarse meshes by building the hierarchy through arbitrary mesh agglomeration.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports efficient iterative solution of conforming finite element systems on complex domains without constructing conforming coarse meshes.
method: Precondition fine-mesh conforming Lagrangian FEM with a coarse polytopal DG or hybrid high-order discretisation.
Build subsequent multigrid levels by further agglomeration.
Transfer coarse solutions using element-wise interpolation and nodal averaging, with local potential reconstruction for the hybrid high-order variant.
evidence_signal: Two- and three-dimensional experiments on structured and unstructured meshes with automatically clustered agglomerates confirm robustness; proven condition-number bounds scale as O((H/h)^3), improving to O((H/h)^2) for DG with appropriately scaled penalty.
watch_item: The condition-number bounds worsen with the coarsening ratio H/h, so aggressive agglomeration can affect solver performance.
paper_title: Geometric Multigrid Preconditioners for conforming Finite Element Methods on Arbitrarily Agglomerated Meshes
